# Job Chapter 9 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 419r–419v

---

**9:1** And-answered Iyyov and-said:

**9:2** "Truly [omnam] I-know [yada'tiy] that [it is] so [ken];
but-how [u-mah] can-a-man [enosh] be-righteous [yitsddaq] with God [im el]?

**9:3** If he-desires [yachpots] to-contend [lariv] with-him,
he-cannot answer-him [lo ya'anennu] one from-a-thousand [achat mi-elef].

**9:4** Wise [chakham] of-heart [levav] and-mighty [ammits] of-strength [koach] —
who has-hardened [hiqshah] [himself] against-him and-remained-whole [vayyishlam]?

**9:5** Who-removes [ha-ma'tiq] mountains [harim] and-they-know-not [ve-lo yade'u],
who overturns-them [hafakham] in-his-anger [be-appo].

**9:6** Who-shakes [ha-margiz] the-earth [erets] from-its-place [mi-meqomah],
and-its-pillars [ammudeiha] tremble [yitpallatsun].

**9:7** Who-speaks [ha-omer] to-the-sun [la-cheresh] and-it-does-not rise [ve-lo yizrach],
and-around-the-stars [ba'ad kokhavim] he-seals [yachtom].

**9:8** Who-stretches-out [noteh] the-heavens [shamayim] by-himself [le-vaddo],
and-treads [ve-dorekh] upon the-heights [bamotei] of-the-sea [yam].

**9:9** Who-makes [oseh] the-Bear [ash], Orion [kesil], and-the-Pleiades [kimah],
and-the-chambers of-the-south [chadrei teman].

**9:10** Who-does great-things [gedolot] beyond searching-out [ad ein cheqer],
and-wonders [nifla'ot] beyond number [ad ein mispar].

**9:11** Behold, he-passes [ya'avor] over-me [alay] and-I-do-not see [ve-lo er'eh],
and-he-moves-on [yachalof] and-I-do-not perceive-him [ve-lo avin lo].

**9:12** Behold, he-snatches-away [yachtof] — who will-restore [yeshivennu]?
Who will-say [yomar] to-him, 'What are-you-doing [mah ta'aseh]?'

**9:13** God [eloah] will-not turn-back [lo yashiv] his-anger [appo];
beneath him bow [shachechu] the-helpers [ozerei] of-Rahab [rahav].

**9:14** How-much-less [af ki] can-I answer-him [a'anennu],
[or] choose [evcharah] my-words [devaray] with-him?

**9:15** Whom [asher] — though I-were-righteous [tsadaqtiy] — I-would-not answer [lo e'eneh];
to-my-judge [li-mshoptiy] I-would-plead-for-grace [etchannan].

**9:16** If I-called [qaratiy] and-he-answered-me [vayya'aneniy],
I-would-not believe [lo a'amin] that he-would-listen [ya'azin] to-my-voice [qoliy].

**9:17** For with-a-tempest [bi-se'arah] he-crushes-me [yeshufeniy],
and-multiplies [ve-hirbah] my-wounds [fetsay'ai] without-cause [chinam].

**9:18** He-does-not permit-me [lo yittenenniy] to-catch my-breath [hashev ruchiy],
for he-fills-me [yasbi'aniy] with-bitterness [mamerorim].

**9:19** If [it is a matter] of-strength [le-koach] — behold the-mighty-one [ammits];
and-if of-justice [le-mishpat] — who will-summon-me [yo'ideniy]?

**9:20** If I-am-righteous [etsdaq], my-mouth [piy] would-condemn-me [yarshi'eniy];
[if I am] blameless [tam ani], he-would-declare-me perverse [ya'aqsheniy].

**9:21** I [am] blameless [tam] — I-do-not know [lo eda] my-soul [nafshiy];
I-despise [em'as] my-life [chayyay].

**9:22** It [is] all-one [achat hiy]; therefore I-say [amartiy]:
the-blameless [tam] and-the-wicked [rasha] he-destroys [hu mekhalleh].

**9:23** If a-scourge [shot] kills [yamit] suddenly [pit'om],
at-the-trial [le-massat] of-the-innocent [neqiyyim] he-mocks [yil'ag].

**9:24** The-earth [erets] is-given [nittenah] into-the-hand of-the-wicked [rasha];
the-faces of-its-judges [shofteha] he-covers [yekhasseh].
If not [im lo] — then who [is] it [hu efo]?

**9:25** And-my-days are-swifter [qallu] than-a-runner [mi-rats];
they-flee [barechu] — they-have-not seen [lo ra'u] good [tovah].

**9:26** They-pass-by [chalefu] with [im] boats of-reed [oniyyot eveh];
like-an-eagle [ke-nesher] that-swoops [yatush] on food [al okhel].

**9:27** If I-say [omriy], 'I-will-forget [eshkechah] my-complaint [sichiy],
I-will-abandon [e'ezvah] my-face [panay] and-I-will-be-cheerful [ve-abliyah],'

**9:28** I-dread [yagoretiy] all my-sufferings [atsetvotay];
I-know that you-will-not hold-me-innocent [lo tenaqeniy].

**9:29** I [am] to-be-condemned [ersha]; why [lammah] then [zeh]
in-vain [hevel] do-I-toil [iyga]?

**9:30** If I-wash-myself [rachatsetiy] with-snow [be-mei shaleg],
and-cleanse [hazikkotiy] my-hands [kapay] with-lye [be-bor],

**9:31** then in-a-pit [be-shachath] you-would-plunge-me [titbeleniy],
and-my-garments [salmotay] would-abhor-me [ti'avuniy].

**9:32** For he-is-not [ki lo] a-man [ish] like-me [kammoniy] that I-should-answer-him [e'enennu],
that we-should-come [navo] together [yachdav] in-judgment [ba-mishpat].

**9:33** There-is-not [lo yesh] between-us [beinenu] an-arbiter [mokhiach],
who-would-lay [yasheth] his-hand [yado] upon us-both [al shenenu].

**9:34** Let-him-take-away [yaser] his-rod [shivto] from-upon-me [me-alay],
and-his-dread [eimatoh] let-it-not terrify-me [al tevatteniy].

**9:35** [Then] I-would-speak [adabberah] and-not fear-him [ve-lo ira'ennu],
for not so [ki lo ken] [am] I with-myself [immadiy]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.8 — "treads upon the heights of the sea":** The verb *dorekh* (to tread) upon *bamotei yam* (the heights/backs of the sea) depicts YHWH as a cosmic warrior who tramples the primordial sea. This imagery is shared with Canaanite and Mesopotamian creation myths.

**v.13 — "helpers of Rahab":** *Rahav* (not the woman of Jericho) is the primordial chaos dragon, and her "helpers" (*ozerei*) are the forces of cosmic disorder. Even these bow before God — how then can Iyyov hope to stand?

**v.33 — "arbiter" (*mokhiach*):** This is one of the most theologically significant words in the book. Iyyov longs for a mediator, someone who could stand between God and man and impose fairness on the dispute. This longing will intensify through the book, reaching its climax in the *go'el* (redeemer) of 19:25.

---
*— EMET*
